Associated Press reporting said Trump’s financial statements were key to approving a $125 million Doral loan in 2011 and a $107 million Chicago loan in 2012. The bank also made its own adjustments to some property valuations. The report does not substantiate the separate allegation that Trump double-billed expenses through internal loans.
proposal.description_long: A retired Deutsche Bank risk management officer, Nicholas Haigh, testified on October 11, 2023, at Donald Trump’s New York civil-fraud trial about the role of Trump’s financial statements in lending decisions. Associated Press reporting, published by PBS NewsHour and other outlets, said the statements were important to approval of a $125 million loan for the Doral golf resort in 2011 and a $107 million loan for the Chicago hotel and tower in 2012. Haigh also described internal review: the bank did not undertake full independent appraisals of every property, but it reduced some valuations supplied by Trump for lending purposes. The AP account described earlier judicial findings concerning the financial statements while identifying Haigh’s statements as trial testimony, rather than treating his evidence as a separate court ruling. The frozen entry’s stronger assertion that Trump double-billed project expenses through internal loans was not established by this report and is excluded. The record therefore covers what the banker testified about loan applications and bank review, without claiming the source proved the unrelated double-billing mechanism.
